claim: In solid tumors, targeted treatments can lead to dramatic regressions, but responses are often short-lived because resistant cancer cells arise.
source_text: In solid tumors, targeted treatments can lead to dramatic regressions, but responses are often short-lived because resistant cancer cells arise.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about targeted cancer therapy outcomes and is supported by the citations provided in the introduction section.

claim: The major strategy proposed for overcoming resistance is combination therapy.
source_text: The major strategy proposed for overcoming resistance is combination therapy.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established scientific consensus in the field of cancer therapeutics.

claim: Dual therapy results in long-term disease control for most patients, if there are no single mutations that cause cross-resistance to both drugs.
source_text: We find that dual therapy results in long-term disease control for most patients, if there are no single mutations that cause cross-resistance to both drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the mathematical model applied to patient data, supported by computational analysis and simulations.

claim: In patients with large disease burden, triple therapy is needed.
source_text: in patients with large disease burden, triple therapy is needed
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is derived from the mathematical model's predictions based on tumor burden data from patients.

claim: Simultaneous therapy with two drugs is much more effective than sequential therapy.
source_text: We also find that simultaneous therapy with two drugs is much more effective than sequential therapy.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is supported by mathematical modeling results shown in Figure 5 and analytical calculations.

claim: Imatinib initiated the current wave of excitement about targeted cancer therapy through its success in treating chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).
source_text: The current wave of excitement about targeted cancer therapy (Sawyers, 2004; Sequist et al., 2008; Kwak et al., 2010; Chapman et al., 2011; Gonzalez-Angulo et al., 2011) was initiated by the success of imatinib in the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) (Druker et al., 2006; Gambacorti-Passerini et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This historical claim is supported by citations to published literature documenting imatinib's success.

claim: Four decades of research passed between the discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and the first treatment to target an activated oncogene in a human cancer.
source_text: Four decades of research passed between the discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and the first treatment to target an activated oncogene in a human cancer.
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact about the timeline of cancer research.

claim: In most patients with solid tumors, the cancer evolves to become resistant within a few months.
source_text: In most patients with solid tumors, the cancer evolves to become resistant within a few months (Amado et al., 2008; Sequist et al., 2008; Gerber and Minna, 2010; Chapman et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies documenting resistance development timelines.

claim: A small number of cells resistant to any targeted agent are always present in large solid tumors at the start of therapy.
source_text: One of the most important conclusions of these studies is that a small number of cells resistant to any targeted agent are always present in large solid tumors at the start of therapy
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from previous theoretical and experimental studies cited in the text.

claim: Resistant cells clonally expand once therapy is administered.
source_text: these cells clonally expand once therapy is administered
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies and represents established understanding of resistance mechanisms.

claim: Tumor recurrences are a fait accompli when single agents are delivered.
source_text: Tumor recurrences are thus a fait accompli when single agents are delivered (Diaz et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is supported by citation to a study and follows from the previous claims about preexisting resistance.

claim: The study analyzed 68 index lesions in 20 melanoma patients receiving vemurafenib.
source_text: To obtain key parameters for our model, we have studied the dynamics of 68 index lesions in 20 melanoma patients receiving the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the actual dataset collected and analyzed in the study.

claim: The average net growth rate of melanoma lesions is 0.01 per day.
source_text: Using these data, we calculate the average net growth rate of these lesions to be 0.01 per day, which is consistent with previous reports (Friberg and Mattson, 1997; Eskelin et al., 2000).
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the study's dataset and validated against previous literature.

claim: The estimated average time between cell divisions in melanoma cells is 7 days.
source_text: The estimated average time between cell divisions in the absence of cell death in melanoma cells is 7 days (Rew and Wilson, 2000)
evidence_reasoning: This parameter is obtained from a cited reference.

claim: The birth (cell division) rate of melanoma cells is b = 0.14 per day.
source_text: implying a birth (cell division) rate of b = 0.14 per day
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the time between cell divisions (1/7 days ≈ 0.14 per day).

claim: The expected number of resistant cells at treatment start in a lesion with M cells is X ≈ M n12 µ when n12 ≥ 1.
source_text: If there is at least one possible mutation that could in principle confer resistance to both drugs, n12 ≥ 1, then X ≈ M n12 µ.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived mathematically from the branching process model as shown in the manuscript.

claim: When there is at least one cross-resistance mutation possible, the expected number of cells resistant to both drugs is independent of the numbers of mutations that confer resistance to each individual drug.
source_text: In this case, the expected number of cells resistant to both drugs is independent of the numbers of mutations, n1 and n2, that have the potential to confer resistance to each individual drug.
evidence_reasoning: This follows from the mathematical formula X ≈ M n12 µ, which does not depend on n1 or n2.

claim: Tumor cells are much more likely to become resistant to dual therapy through one mutation conferring resistance to both drugs simultaneously than through sequential mutations conferring resistance to each drug separately.
source_text: Intuitively, this means that tumor cells are much more likely to become resistant to dual therapy through the occurrence of one mutation conferring resistance to both drugs simultaneously than through sequential mutations conferring resistance to each drug separately.
evidence_reasoning: This is explained as an intuitive interpretation of the mathematical results comparing single-step vs two-step resistance pathways.

claim: When there is no cross-resistance (n12 = 0), the expected number of resistant cells is X ≈ M n1n2 µ².
source_text: If there is no mutation that could confer resistance to both drugs simultaneously (no cross-resistance), then n12 = 0 and we obtain X ≈ M n1n2 µ2.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical model when cross-resistance mutations are not possible.

claim: The expected number of cells resistant to combination therapy with k drugs, with no cross-resistance, is X ≈ M n1n2 … nk µk.
source_text: In general, the expected number of cells resistant to combination therapy with k drugs, with no cross-resistance, is X ≈ M n1n2 … nk µk (proof in Supplementary file 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is a generalization of the mathematical model to k drugs, with proof provided in supplementary materials.

claim: The 68 lesions in the dataset declined at a median rate of -0.03 per day during vemurafenib treatment.
source_text: To obtain estimates for the birth rate b′ and death rate d′ of sensitive cells during treatment, we calculate that the 68 lesions in our dataset declined at median rate b′ − d′ = −0.03 per day (−0.01 and −0.07 being 10th and 90th percentile, respectively).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct calculation from the study's dataset of melanoma patients.

claim: Monotherapy leads to temporary tumor shrinkage but is always followed by tumor regrowth for clinically detectable tumor sizes.
source_text: For clinically detectable sizes (M = 1010, 109, 108, depending on the location of the tumors and the detection methods used), monotherapy leads to a temporary shrinkage of the tumor but is always followed by tumor regrowth.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through simulations shown in Figure 2A-C based on the mathematical model.

claim: Treatment failure can be caused either by preexistence of resistance to both drugs or the emergence of resistant cells during treatment.
source_text: In summary, treatment failure can be caused either by the preexistence of resistance to both drugs in a small number of tumor cells (Figure 2E) or the emergence of resistant cells during treatment (Figure 2F).
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from the simulation results shown in Figure 2 and the mathematical model.

claim: Monotherapy will fail in all 22 patients studied with metastatic disease.
source_text: We find that monotherapy will fail in all 22 patients (Table 1 and Supplementary file 3)
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated using equation (1) applied to the tumor burden data from 22 patients.

claim: If there is even one possible mutation that can confer resistance to both drugs, dual therapy has only a small chance of curing patients.
source_text: If there is even one possible mutation that can in principle confer resistance to both drugs, then our model shows that dual therapy has also only a small chance of curing patients, even those with the smallest tumor burden.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through calculations shown in Table 1 for the 22-patient cohort.

claim: None of the 22 patients are expected to be cured by dual therapy when there is one cross-resistance mutation possible.
source_text: In our cohort of 22 patients, none are expected to be cured under these circumstances (Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model applied to patient data, shown in Table 1.

claim: Eight patients with the smallest tumor burden would have >95% probability of cure with dual therapy when there are no cross-resistance mutations.
source_text: In the cohort described in Table 1, we calculate that eight patients (those with the smallest tumor burden) would have >95% probability of cure.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated using the mathematical model for the scenario with n12 = 0, as shown in Table 1.

claim: Patients with the largest tumor burden would still have a >20% probability of tumor recurrence even with dual therapy without cross-resistance.
source_text: Those with the largest tumor burden would still have a >20% probability of tumor recurrence.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model for patients with high tumor burden in the n12 = 0 scenario.

claim: Therapy with three agents will not cure patients if there is even one mutation that can confer resistance to all three agents.
source_text: Additional simulations show that therapy with three agents will also not cure patients if there is even one mutation that can confer resistance to all three agents.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through additional computer simulations extending the dual therapy model.

claim: The number of metastatic lesions in the 22 patients ranged from 1 to 30.
source_text: The number of metastatic lesions in the 22 patients described in Table 1 ranged from 1 to 30
evidence_reasoning: This is direct observational data from radiographic quantification of patient metastases.

claim: The total tumor burden in the 22 patients ranged from 9 × 10^8 to 3 × 10^11 cells.
source_text: their total tumor burden ranged from 9 × 108 to 3 × 1011 cells
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from radiographic measurements of metastatic lesions in the patient cohort.

claim: Sequential combination therapy will 'always' fail when there is a possibility of a single mutation conferring resistance to both drugs.
source_text: When there is a possibility of a single mutation conferring resistance to both drugs, sequential combination therapy will 'always' fail.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through mathematical modeling and simulations shown in Figure 5.

claim: In approximately 74% of lesions treated sequentially, failure is due to mutations present prior to treatment with the first drug.
source_text: In ∼74% of lesions, the failure is due to mutations that were present prior to the treatment with the first drug
evidence_reasoning: This percentage is calculated from simulations of sequential therapy shown in Figure 5.

claim: In approximately 26% of lesions treated sequentially, failure is due to development of cells resistant to drug 2 during treatment with drug 1.
source_text: whereas in ∼26% of the lesions, failure is due to the development of cells resistant to drug 2 during treatment with drug 1
evidence_reasoning: This percentage is calculated from simulations of sequential therapy dynamics.

claim: With simultaneous therapy, 26.3% of patients can be cured when there is one cross-resistance mutation.
source_text: With simultaneous therapy, 26.3% of patients can be cured under the same circumstances.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the mathematical model comparing simultaneous vs sequential therapy, shown in Figure 5B.

claim: If two drugs have no resistance mutations in common (n12 = 0), simultaneous therapy is successful with a probability of 99.9%.
source_text: If the two drugs have no resistance mutations in common (n12 = 0), then simultaneous therapy is successful with a probability of 99.9%
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the model for the no cross-resistance scenario, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Sequential therapy fails in all cases when there are no cross-resistance mutations.
source_text: while sequential therapy still fails in all cases
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through simulations shown in Figure 5D even when n12 = 0.

claim: Cancer stem cells in CML represent only 0.1% of cancer cells.
source_text: The fraction of cancer stem cells appears to be this low in CML
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as an established fact about CML, implicitly supported by the citation to Michor et al., 2005.

claim: In solid tumors, the fraction of cancer stem cells is usually higher than 5% and in some cases close to 100%.
source_text: In solid tumors, however, the fraction of cancer stem cells seems much higher, usually higher than 5% and in some cases close to 100% (Shackleton et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Shackleton et al., 2009.

claim: Non-stem cells can convert to cancer stem cells under certain conditions.
source_text: This issue is further complicated by the fact that the situation is plastic, with non-stem cells converting to cancer stem cells under certain conditions (Gupta et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Gupta et al., 2009.

claim: If each resistance mutation decreases the net growth rate of cells by 10%, the probability that dual therapy with no cross-resistance will eradicate a lesion of size 10^11 with daily cell division is 68%.
source_text: For example, if each resistance mutation decreases the net growth rate of cells by 10%, the probability that dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations will eradicate a lesion of size 1011 in which cells divide on average every day is 68% (compared with 47% in the case of neutral resistance).
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from simulations incorporating costly resistance, shown in Table 2.

claim: The rate b′ − d′ of tumor decline is of primary importance for treatment outcomes.
source_text: Overall, the rate b′ − d′ of tumor decline is of primary importance
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from analysis of the mathematical model under different scenarios.

claim: Whether tumor decline is achieved by eliminating cells or suppressing division has only a minor effect on treatment outcomes.
source_text: whether this is achieved by eliminating cells or suppressing division has only a minor effect on treatment outcomes
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through comparison of different treatment mechanisms in the model, with example calculations provided.

claim: If there is one genetic alteration that can confer resistance to two targeted agents, therapy with those agents will not result in sustained benefit for the majority of patients with advanced disease.
source_text: Most importantly, they show that even if there is one genetic alteration within any of the 6.6 billion base pairs present in a human diploid cell that can confer resistance to two targeted agents, therapy with those agents will not result in sustained benefit for the majority of patients with advanced disease.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion drawn from the mathematical modeling and patient data analysis presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: If there is the possibility of a mutation conferring cross-resistance to three drugs, lesions of the size commonly observed in patients with advanced cancers will always recur.
source_text: The same result is obtained with triple therapy; if there is the possibility of a mutation conferring cross-resistance to three drugs, lesions of the size commonly observed in patients with advanced cancers will always recur.
evidence_reasoning: This extends the dual therapy findings to triple therapy through additional simulations and mathematical analysis.

claim: Increased expression of growth factors such as hepatocyte growth factor can confer resistance to a variety of drugs that inhibit kinases functioning through different pathways.
source_text: For example, it has been shown that the increased expression of growth factors (such as hepatocyte growth factor) can confer resistance to a variety of drugs that inhibit kinases functioning through different pathways (Straussman et al., 2012; Wilson et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Straussman et al., 2012 and Wilson et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in genes encoding ABC transporters can confer resistance to many different drugs.
source_text: Moreover, it is well known that mutations in several different genes, including those encoding ABC transporters, can confer resistance to many different drugs (Lavi et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as well-known knowledge and supported by citation to Lavi et al., 2012.

claim: The results are not readily applicable to therapies that rely on immune destruction of tumors.
source_text: Our results are not readily applicable to therapies that rely on the immune destruction of tumors (Kirkwood et al., 2012), such as those employing CTLA-4 (Hodi et al., 2010), PD1 (Topalian et al., 2012), or CD19-CARs (Grupp et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors based on the nature of their model.

claim: The immune system, unlike small molecule compounds, can replicate and evolve.
source_text: The immune system, unlike small molecule compounds, can replicate and evolve
evidence_reasoning: This is a fundamental biological fact about the immune system.

claim: Long-term control of disease is more common with immune modulators than with small molecule drugs.
source_text: why long-term control of disease is more common with these therapies than with small molecule drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is implied by the discussion of differences between immunotherapy and small molecule therapy outcomes.

claim: Sequential administration of targeted agents precludes any chance for cure even when there are no possible mutations that can confer cross-resistance.
source_text: Our data show that this sequential administration precludes any chance for cure—even when there are no possible mutations that can confer cross-resistance (Figure 5C).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through the mathematical model and simulations shown in Figure 5C.

claim: When there are potential mutations conferring cross-resistance to two or more agents, simultaneous administration offers some hope for cure while there is no hope with sequential therapy.
source_text: And when there are potential mutations conferring cross-resistance to two or more agents, simultaneous administration offers some hope for cure while there is no hope with sequential therapy (Figure 5A).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through comparison of simultaneous vs sequential therapy in the model, shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The model is based on a multitype branching process.
source_text: Our model is based on a multitype branching process (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence_reasoning: This describes the mathematical framework used to construct the model.

claim: Similar mathematical modeling has successfully predicted the dynamics of acquired resistance in colorectal cancer patients treated with panitumumab.
source_text: Similar mathematical modeling has successfully predicted the dynamics of acquired resistance, including the timing of treatment failure, in colorectal cancer patients treated with the EGFR inhibitor panitumumab (Diaz et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This claim about previous successful predictions is supported by citation to Diaz et al., 2012.

claim: The current work builds on previous studies by using recent advances in the mathematical theory of branching processes.
source_text: Our current work builds on these previous studies by using recent advances in the mathematical theory of branching processes (Antal and Krapivsky, 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This describes how the current work extends previous modeling approaches, citing the mathematical advances used.

claim: The point mutation rate is approximately 10^-9 for most cancers.
source_text: where s = 1 − d/b is the survival probability of the branching process initiated with a single cell and u is the point mutation rate, ∼10−9 for most cancers
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as an established parameter value for cancer mutation rates.

claim: The study quantified all radiographically detectable metastases in 22 patients: 7 with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, 11 with colorectal carcinomas, and 6 with melanomas.
source_text: To determine the total extent of disease in typical patients who enroll for clinical trials, we quantified all radiographically detectable metastases in 22 such patients: 7 with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, 11 with colorectal carcinomas, and 6 with melanomas
evidence_reasoning: This describes the actual data collection performed in the study.

claim: For 21 lesions in the vemurafenib dataset, two pretreatment measurements were available.
source_text: For 21 lesions in our vemurafenib dataset, two pretreatment measurements were available.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the available data used for parameter estimation.

claim: The model assumes birth and death rates remain constant for all cell types prior to treatment.
source_text: For simplicity, we assume that these birth and death rates remain constant for all cell types prior to treatment
evidence_reasoning: This is an explicit modeling assumption stated by the authors.

claim: The model neglects variations in growth rate due to spatial and metabolic constraints in solid tumors.
source_text: and neglect variations in the growth rate due to spatial and metabolic constraints in solid tumors (Bozic et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is an explicit simplifying assumption of the model.

claim: A cell type is defined as sensitive if the treatment would cause its death rate to exceed its birth rate.
source_text: A cell type is defined as sensitive if the treatment in question would cause its death rate to exceed its birth rate; otherwise, it is resistant.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition established by the authors for their model.

claim: Drugs in a combination treatment are assumed to be given at concentrations tolerable by patients.
source_text: We assume that drugs in a combination treatment are given at concentrations tolerable by patients
evidence_reasoning: This is an explicit assumption of the model reflecting clinical practice.

claim: Resistant cells maintain pretreatment birth and death rates during treatment.
source_text: We assume that resistant cells maintain the pretreatment birth and death rates, b and d, respectively, during treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This is an explicit modeling assumption about resistant cell behavior.

claim: The typical death rate of sensitive cells during treatment is d′ = b′ + 0.03.
source_text: Thus, we set the typical death rate of sensitive cells during treatment to d′ = b′ + 0.03
evidence_reasoning: This parameter is set based on the median decline rate observed in the dataset.

claim: As a default in simulations, treatment affects only the death rate (b′ = b).
source_text: As a default in our simulations, we suppose that treatment affects only the death rate (b′ = b)
evidence_reasoning: This is an explicit default assumption for the simulations.

claim: The mathematical analysis applies also to the case that treatment affects the birth rate.
source_text: but our mathematical analysis applies also to the case that treatment affects the birth rate
evidence_reasoning: This states the generality of the mathematical framework beyond the default assumption.

claim: Resistance is the outcome of random mutation, division, and death events.
source_text: We emphasize, however, that resistance is the outcome of random mutation, division, and death events
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the stochastic nature of the biological process being modeled.

claim: Resistance may arise in one lesion but not in another, even if these lesions are otherwise identical.
source_text: and consequently may arise in one lesion but not in another, even if these lesions are otherwise identical
evidence_reasoning: This is a consequence of the stochastic nature of resistance development in the model.

claim: For combination therapies with drugs that have resistance mutations in common, the probability of eradicating a lesion is only marginally affected by costly resistance.
source_text: For combination therapies with drugs that have resistance mutations in common, the probability of eradicating a lesion is only marginally affected by costly resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from simulation results shown in Table 2.

claim: For dual therapies with no cross-resistance mutations, treatment has a high chance of eradicating all but the largest lesions, whether or not resistance is costly.
source_text: For dual therapies with no cross-resistance mutations, treatment has a high chance of eradicating all but the largest lesions, whether or not resistance is costly.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from simulation results shown in Table 2.

claim: The parameters with the strongest effects on the success of combination treatments are lesion sizes and point mutation rate.
source_text: The parameters with the strongest effects on the success of combination treatments—apart from the number of cross-resistance mutations—are lesion sizes and point mutation rate.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from sensitivity analysis of the model across different parameter values.

claim: Combination treatments will be more effective in cancers with small fractions of tumor stem cells.
source_text: Thus, we expect that combination treatments will be more effective in cancers with small fractions of tumor stem cells (small effective population size of lesions)
evidence_reasoning: This prediction follows from the model's dependence on effective population size.

claim: Combination treatments will be less effective in cancers with significantly increased point mutation rates.
source_text: and less effective in cancers with significantly increased point mutation rates
evidence_reasoning: This prediction follows from the model's dependence on mutation rate.

claim: The development of drugs that act through distinct pathways will be essential for the success of combination therapies in the clinic.
source_text: The development of drugs that act through distinct pathways will therefore be essential for the success of combination therapies in the clinic.
evidence_reasoning: This recommendation follows from the finding that cross-resistance severely limits treatment success.

claim: Drugs that have very different chemical structures, in addition to distinct mechanisms of action, may be required to circumvent resistance mechanisms.
source_text: Drugs that have very different chemical structures, in addition to distinct mechanisms of action, may be required to circumvent these resistance mechanisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative recommendation based on the challenges of avoiding cross-resistance identified in the study.

claim: Long-term control of disease is more common with immune modulators than with small molecule drugs.
source_text: why long-term control of disease is more common with these therapies than with small molecule drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as an observed clinical phenomenon that the authors acknowledge but do not model.

claim: The model uses Monte Carlo computer simulations to confirm analytical results.
source_text: We use Monte Carlo computer simulations to confirm our analytical results and improve our understanding of the evolutionary dynamics during cancer treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational methodology used to validate the mathematical model.

claim: Between 10^6 and 10^8 simulation runs are used for each parameter combination.
source_text: Between 106 and 108 runs are used for each parameter combination.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational effort invested in the simulations.

claim: In the case of large lesions with high cell turnover rates, even dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations would be expected to fail in 37% of patients.
source_text: We note that in patients whose tumors have high cell turnover (time between cell divisions of 1 day, corresponding to b = 1), even dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations would be expected to fail in 37% of patients described in Table 1
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from simulations with different parameter values as shown in Supplementary file 3.
